summary:
This change turns a tight origin allowlist into a reflect-any-origin CORS policy while still advertising credentialed access. That is a credentialed cross-origin data leak: a page on any site can `fetch` this API with `credentials: "include"` and the browser will expose the authenticated response.

Native mobile HTTP stacks do not enforce CORS, so they gain nothing from these headers. Mobile webviews do send `Origin` and still need an explicit allowlist of known app origins (the existing app host, plus any Capacitor/Ionic/custom schemes you actually ship). Keep `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` only for those allowlisted origins. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` together with credentials is also invalid in the Fetch spec, so the null-origin fallback is rejected by browsers.

The added `Vary: Origin` header is the right cache signal once reflection is limited to the allowlist.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Head `corsHeaders` always sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to the request Origin (or `*`) together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, removing the base allowlist that only echoed matching origins. That is a real cross-origin credentialed CORS misconfiguration as claimed.
